scenarios.name: Major cyber attack on Australia
scenarios.sa_impact: Banks, payments, hospitals, fuel distribution, telcos and the power grid all run on networks; a large attack can stop card payments and services for hours to days.

scenarios.why: Large attacks are usually preceded by quieter steps: a surge in newly exploited flaws in VPNs and firewalls (how state groups like Volt Typhoon get in), scanning of industrial-control systems, a rise in ransomware victims in the target country, and official warnings. Before Russia's 2022 invasion, wiper malware hit Ukraine a day ahead; Chinese groups have been found pre-positioned in US and allied infrastructure.

scenarios.convergence: Signs are converging across 4 separate areas (ai-enabled hacking, cloud services, fraud waves and synthetic media). Unrelated systems flagging the same scenario at once is the pattern seen before past events. In November 2025 Anthropic reported the first documented AI-orchestrated cyber-espionage campaign: a Chinese state-sponsored group used an AI agent to carry out 80-90% of an attack on about 30 organisations, at thousands of requests per second. A fake AI image of a Pentagon explosion briefly moved US markets in May 2023, and a deepfake video call of a CFO tricked a company into paying US$25 million in 2024. The likely signature of an AI attack is breadth and speed: many unrelated systems and vendors hit at once, synthetic media of officials, and shocks with no clear human cause. The strongest signs not yet showing: exploited flaws across unusually many vendors at once, flash crash or exchange trading halt and market fear index jumps 25%+ in a day.
